question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, egress 205.188.204.187
request.body: one keyless tools/call of aws___retrieve_skill with skill_name aurora-dsql, copied verbatim from a search_documentation result as that tool's description requires, jsonrpc 2.0, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

decoded.what-it-answered: HTTP/2 200, content-type application/json, 39219 bytes, result.isError false. The decoded payload is a single skill_content string of 37407 characters (37557 UTF-8 bytes) whose first line is "# Amazon Aurora DSQL": an AWS-authored agent skill, served whole to an anonymous caller.
decoded.why-this-record-exists: the registry's reviewer refused to let one record claim that all five of this endpoint's tools work keyless when one had been called, and named the condition for the other four: their own measured calls. This is one of those four. It is one request, per the probe schema's own title, "One unauthenticated, unpaid request and what it answered".
decoded.what-it-establishes: aws___retrieve_skill, the name this endpoint's own tools/list advertises, executes for a caller with no credential, no account and no payment, and returns real content rather than a refusal wrapped in a 200. It establishes this for aws___retrieve_skill and for no other tool.
decoded.and-what-it-does-not-establish: nothing about a rate limit: this request was spaced 25 to 26 seconds from its neighbours precisely to avoid the 429 this endpoint answered to a denser sweep on 2026-09-30 (p-20260930-aws-knowledge-mcp-anonymous-429), so the spacing was chosen to dodge a limit, not to measure one. Nothing about the unprefixed-name defect either: the name called here is the prefixed one that works.
decoded.the-status-line-read: the origin's status is the SECOND HTTP line in the captured headers. This container's egress proxy answers CONNECT with its own "HTTP/1.1 200 Connection Established" first; both lines are in the artifact so a reader meets the same trap.
decoded.where-the-argument-came-from: the skill_name aurora-dsql was not invented. It is the rank_order 1 title of a keyless aws___search_documentation call with search_phrase "agent skills" and topics ["agent_skills"], sent at 06:04:51Z, 47 seconds before this one; that request and its four results (aurora-dsql, amazon-workspaces-agent-access, amazon-bedrock, aws-iam) are in the artifact under the heading aws___search_documentation. It is not filed as its own probe record because the tool it exercises is already measured in p-20260930-aws-knowledge-mcp-prefixed-name-serves.
decoded.what-this-means-for-an-agent-reading-the: this endpoint serves AWS-authored agent skills, whole, to a caller with no AWS account. That is a capability a reader of this registry would act on and no record established it before today.

finding: aws___retrieve_skill, called keyless with skill_name aurora-dsql copied verbatim from a search_documentation result as the tool's own description requires, answered HTTP 200 with result.isError false and a 37,407-character skill_content string beginning "# Amazon Aurora DSQL". The AWS Knowledge MCP endpoint serves AWS-authored agent skills, whole, to a caller with no AWS account, no credential and no payment. No record in this registry established that before today, and it is the capability on this endpoint most likely to matter to an agent reading the entry.
